To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the electric field in air showers has both a geomagnetic and a charge-excess component, that the electric field is polarized, and that the polarization of the field is affected by the refractive index of air, the shower geometry, and the shower development.

the polarization of radio pulses emitted by air showers depends on the shower geometry, and that relativistic effects in the refractive index play an important role in the calculation of the radio emission of cosmic ray air showers.

the radio emission from cosmic rays is a very complicated problem that requires the use of a full Monte Carlo code that includes all the details of shower development, and that the polarization of the pulses is a very useful observable for the study of the emission mechanisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of radio emission from extensive air showers, using a full 3D air shower Monte Carlo simulation code.

the development of a tool to study the radio emission from extensive air showers, which is essential for the interpretation of data collected by the radio detection techniques that have been proposed for the next generation of cosmic ray experiments.
the development of a new generation of Monte Carlo codes that can be used to predict the radio signals emitted in extensive air showers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the emission mechanism(s) is (are) complex, and the radio emission of extensive air showers depends on the shower geometry, the refractive index and on the emission mechanism(s).
the radio pulse is not a simple function of the primary energy or zenith angle of the shower.
the radio pulses emitted in air showers are very rich in information about shower geometry and composition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the radio pulse emission is not just a geometrical effect.

ZHAireS can be used for the prediction of radio pulses in the frequency range from 10 to 100 MHz, for showers with energies from 10 ^{16}  eV up to 10 ^{19}  eVs, and for zenith angles from 0° to 60°.
the radio pulses are sensitive to the geometry and the refractive index of the shower and, therefore, can be used to probe the atmospheric conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the radio emission of an extensive air shower is a very complex phenomenon, and that the electric field of the pulse is highly sensitive to the shower parameters and geometry.
the radio emission of extensive air showers can only be understood by taking into account the full shower development in the Earth’s atmosphere.
the radio pulse is sensitive to the shower geometry and the refractive index, and that these two effects are intimately coupled.
